findings.title: Step-1 neutral derelict (orbitR 0) fails the new §6.2 validation, so step-1 snapshots cannot restore
findings.claim: §6.3 step 1 zeroes the derelict (`derelict zeroed with salvaged 1`), so `derelict.orbitR` is 0. §6.2 validates `derelict.orbitR in the drawn bands` ([700, 1000] ∪ [1400, 1599]). Every snapshot taken under step 1 would therefore fail validation on restore. The two sections contradict each other.
findings.evidence: spec L117 (step 1: derelict zeroed, salvaged 1); spec L113 (orbitR in the drawn bands); spec L68 (bands 700..1000, 1400..1599); src/renderer/src/sim/duel/modules.ts:L87-L95 (the snapshot path runs through these modules)
findings.why: Under step 1 the snapshot and online-join tests would throw. The plan author would then have to choose between relaxing validation and picking a non-zero neutral value, and those two choices give different step-1 hashes.
findings.fix: Pick one neutral value that the validation accepts, and name it in step 1. One option is `orbitR` 700 with `salvaged` 1. The other is to allow `orbitR` 0 in validation only when `salvaged` is 1. Then add a step-1 snapshot round-trip test.

findings.title: The spec doesn't say whether `scanner` is computed before or after contactScan admission, and a takeover in the same tick depends on it
findings.claim: §4.6 says step.ts sets `scanner = scan.contact < 0 || attendant(d, scan.by) >= 0` 'after the seat phase'. §5's admission phase also runs after the seat phase and can change `scan.by`: a faster seat takes over the rate and its `by`. Take a Helm scan whose Helm player stands this tick while Science sends contactScan on the same contact. If `scanner` is computed before admission it is false and the scan cancels. If it is computed after, it is true and the scan continues at Science's rate.
findings.evidence: spec L82 (scanner computed 'after the seat phase'); spec L92 (takeover sets `by`); spec L97 (admission after the throttle loop, against the seats after the seat phase); src/renderer/src/sim/duel/step.ts:L168-L192 (crew ShipInput built, then the command loops)
findings.why: The two orders produce different hashes in a reachable case, and the scan tests ('a faster seat takes over', 'leaving the seat cancels') would be written against whichever one the implementer guessed.
findings.fix: State that `scanner` is computed after the contactScan admission loop, from the scan as it stands after admission. Add a test where the Helm player stands and Science takes over in the same tick.

verified: Hostility triggers line up with the event shapes: a `laser` event has `ship` and `hit` (state.ts:L78) and a `missileEnd` event has `ship` and `target` (state.ts:L80). The hostility step runs after resolveMissiles and tickWeapons (duel.ts:L33-L34), so that tick's events are present.
Holding the Patrol shield clock fits tickWeapons L106-L107. A layer at layers + 1 is never regained because the `shields >= layers` branch zeroes the clock.
A derelict at orbitR ≤ 1599 is always at least 401 from spawns at SPAWN_RADIUS 2000 (tuning.ts:L34). The 600 rule can bind only on the outer band, and the inner band always clears it.
DUEL_MODULES uses path 'tactical' for the tactical modules (modules.ts:L88-L89), and the `science` id doesn't collide with an existing module id.
